local AdjacencyMatrix = {}
AdjacencyMatrix.__index = AdjacencyMatrix

function AdjacencyMatrix.__tostring(self: AdjacencyMatrix)
	local s = "\n"

	for i = 1, self.length do
		if i == 1 then
			s ..= "\n"
		end

		local sub = ""
		for j = 1, self.width do
			if j == self.width then
				sub ..= `{self.matrix[i][j]}`
				continue
			end

			sub ..= `{self.matrix[i][j]}, `
		end

		sub ..= "\n"
		s ..= sub
	end

	return s
end

function AdjacencyMatrix.extend(self: AdjacencyMatrix)
	self.length = self.length + 1
	self.width = self.length + 1

	self.matrix[self.length] = {}
	for j = 1, self.width do
		self.matrix[self.length][j] = 0
	end

	for i = 1, self.length do
		self.matrix[i][self.width] = 0
	end
end

function AdjacencyMatrix.setEdge(
	self: AdjacencyMatrix,
	i: number,
	j: number,
	val: number
)
	self.matrix[i][j] = val
end

function AdjacencyMatrix.toAdjacencyList(self: AdjacencyMatrix): { { number } }
	local list = {}

	for i = 1, self.length do
		list[i] = {}
		for j = 1, self.width do
			if self.matrix[i][j] ~= 0 then
				table.insert(list[i], j)
			end
		end
	end

	return list
end

function AdjacencyMatrix.topologicalSort(self: AdjacencyMatrix): { number }?
	local adjacencyList = self:toAdjacencyList()

	local result = {}
	local inDegrees = table.create(self.length, 0)

	for i = 1, self.length do
		for _, j in adjacencyList[i] do
			inDegrees[j] += 1
		end
	end

	local queue = {}
	for i = 1, self.length do
		if inDegrees[i] == 0 then
			table.insert(queue, i)
		end
	end

	while #queue ~= 0 do
		local i = table.remove(queue, 1) :: number
		table.insert(result, i)

		for _, j in adjacencyList[i] do
			inDegrees[j] -= 1
			if inDegrees[j] == 0 then
				table.insert(queue, j)
			end
		end
	end

	if #result ~= self.length then
		return nil
	end

	return result
end

function AdjacencyMatrix.new(): AdjacencyMatrix
	return setmetatable({
		matrix = {},
		length = 0,
		width = 0,
	}, AdjacencyMatrix)
end

export type AdjacencyMatrix = setmetatable<{
	matrix: { { number } },
	length: number,
	width: number,
}, typeof(AdjacencyMatrix)>

local DependencyGraph = {}
DependencyGraph.__index = DependencyGraph

function DependencyGraph.getOrderedList<T>(self: DependencyGraph<T>): { T }?
	local orderedList = {}

	local topologicalSort = self.matrix:topologicalSort()
	if not topologicalSort then
		return nil
	end

	for _, i in topologicalSort do
		table.insert(orderedList, self.nodes[i])
	end

	return orderedList
end

function DependencyGraph.insertBefore<T>(
	self: DependencyGraph<T>,
	node: T,
	beforeNode: T
)
	local i = table.find(self.nodes, beforeNode)
	assert(i, "Node not found in DependencyGraph:insertBefore(_, unknown)")

	local j = table.find(self.nodes, node)
	if not j then
		table.insert(self.nodes, node)
		j = #self.nodes
	end

	-- selene: allow(incorrect_standard_library_use)
	assert(j)

	self.matrix:extend()
	self.matrix:setEdge(j, i, 1)

	return self
end

function DependencyGraph.insertAfter<T>(
	self: DependencyGraph<T>,
	node: T,
	afterNode: T
)
	local i = table.find(self.nodes, afterNode)
	assert(i, "Node not found in DependencyGraph:insertAfter(_, unknown)")

	local j = table.find(self.nodes, node)
	if not j then
		table.insert(self.nodes, node)
		j = #self.nodes
	end

	-- selene: allow(incorrect_standard_library_use)
	assert(j)

	self.matrix:extend()
	self.matrix:setEdge(i, j, 1)

	return self
end

function DependencyGraph.insert<T>(self: DependencyGraph<T>, node: T)
	local i = #self.nodes
	table.insert(self.nodes, node)
	local j = #self.nodes

	self.matrix:extend()

	if i ~= 0 then
		self.matrix:setEdge(i, j, 1)
	end

	return self
end

function DependencyGraph.new(): DependencyGraph<any>
	return setmetatable({
		nodes = {},
		matrix = AdjacencyMatrix.new(),
		length = 0,
		width = 0,
	}, DependencyGraph)
end

export type DependencyGraph<T> = setmetatable<{
	nodes: { T },
	matrix: AdjacencyMatrix,
	length: number,
	width: number,
}, typeof(DependencyGraph)>

return DependencyGraph

--- @class Phase
---
--- Phases represent tags that tell the scheduler when to
--- schedule a set of systems.
local Phase = {}
Phase.__index = Phase

function Phase.__tostring(self: Phase)
	return self._name
end

--- @within Phase
---
--- Creates a new Phase, with an optional name to use for debugging.
--- When no name is provided, the script and line number will be used.
function Phase.new(name: string?): Phase
	name = name or debug.info(2, "sl") :: string
	return setmetatable({
		_name = name,
		_type = "phase",
	}, Phase)
end

--- @prop PreStartup Phase
--- @within Phase
--- Runs before the `Startup` Phase.

--- @prop Startup Phase
--- @within Phase
--- This Phase will run once, the first time the Scheduler is ran,
--- before any other Phases are ran.

--- @prop PostStartup Phase
--- @within Phase
--- Runs after the `Startup` phase.

Phase.PreStartup = Phase.new("PreStartup")
Phase.Startup = Phase.new("Startup")
Phase.PostStartup = Phase.new("PostStartup")

export type Phase = setmetatable<{
	_name: string,
	_type: "phase",
}, typeof(Phase)>

return Phase

local DependencyGraph = require(script.Parent.DependencyGraph)
local Phase = require(script.Parent.Phase)

type DependencyGraph<T> = DependencyGraph.DependencyGraph<T>
type Phase = Phase.Phase

--- @class Pipeline
---
--- Pipelines represent a set of ordered Phases. Systems cannot be
--- assigned to Pipelines themselves, but rather to Phases within
--- those Pipelines.
local Pipeline = {}
Pipeline.__index = Pipeline

function Pipeline.__tostring(self: Pipeline): string
	return self._name
end

--- @method insert
--- @within Pipeline
--- @param phase Phase
--- @return Pipeline
---
--- Adds a Phase to the Pipeline, ordering it implicitly.
function Pipeline.insert(self: Pipeline, phase: Phase): Pipeline
	self.dependencyGraph:insert(phase)
	return self
end

--- @method insertAfter
--- @within Pipeline
--- @param phase Phase
--- @param after Phase
--- @return Pipeline
---
--- Adds a Phase to the Pipeline after another Phase, ordering it explicitly.
function Pipeline.insertAfter(
	self: Pipeline,
	phase: Phase,
	afterPhase: Phase
): Pipeline
	local i = table.find(self.dependencyGraph.nodes, afterPhase)
	assert(
		i,
		"Unknown Phase in Pipeline:insertAfter(_, unknown), try adding this Phase to the Pipeline."
	)

	self.dependencyGraph:insertAfter(phase, afterPhase)
	return self
end

--- @method insertBefore
--- @within Pipeline
--- @param phase Phase
--- @param before Phase
--- @return Pipeline
---
--- Adds a Phase to the Pipeline before another Phase, ordering it explicitly.
function Pipeline.insertBefore(
	self: Pipeline,
	phase: Phase,
	beforePhase: Phase
): Pipeline
	local i = table.find(self.dependencyGraph.nodes, beforePhase)
	assert(
		i,
		"Unknown Phase in Pipeline:insertBefore(_, unknown), try adding this Phase to the Pipeline."
	)

	self.dependencyGraph:insertBefore(phase, beforePhase)
	return self
end

--- @within Pipeline
---
--- Creates a new Pipeline, with an optional name to use for debugging.
--- When no name is provided, the script and line number will be used.
function Pipeline.new(name: string?): Pipeline
	name = name or debug.info(2, "sl") :: string

	local dependencyGraph: DependencyGraph<Phase> = DependencyGraph.new()

	return setmetatable({
		_name = name,
		_type = "pipeline",
		dependencyGraph = dependencyGraph,
	}, Pipeline)
end

--- @prop Startup Pipeline
--- @within Pipeline
---
--- A Pipeline containing the `PreStartup`, `Startup`, and `PostStartup` phases.
Pipeline.Startup = Pipeline.new()
	:insert(Phase.PreStartup)
	:insert(Phase.Startup)
	:insert(Phase.PostStartup)

export type Pipeline = setmetatable<{
	_name: string,
	_type: "pipeline",
	dependencyGraph: DependencyGraph<Phase>,
}, typeof(Pipeline)>

return Pipeline

--- @class Scheduler
---
--- An Object which handles scheduling Systems to run within different
--- Phases. The order of which Systems run will be defined either
--- implicitly by when it was added, or explicitly by tagging the system
--- with a Phase.
local Scheduler = {}
Scheduler.__index = Scheduler

--- @method addPlugin
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param plugin PlanckPlugin
---
--- Initializes a plugin with the scheduler, see the [Plugin Docs](/docs/plugins) for more information.
function Scheduler.addPlugin<T, U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	plugin: setmetatable<{}, BasePlugin<T>>
)
	local _plugin = plugin :: Plugin
	_plugin:build(self)

	table.insert(self._plugins, _plugin)
	return self
end

type PartialHookContext = {
	scheduler: Scheduler<...unknown>,
}

type Hook<T> = {
	__T: T,
}

type Hooks = {
	SystemAdd: Hook<(context: SystemHookContext) -> ()>,
	SystemRemove: Hook<(context: SystemHookContext) -> ()>,
	SystemReplace: Hook<(context: SystemReplaceContext) -> ()>,
	SystemEdited: Hook<(context: SystemEditedContext) -> ()>,
	SystemCleanup: Hook<(context: SystemErrorContext) -> ()>,
	SystemError: Hook<(context: SystemErrorContext) -> ()>,
	SystemTriedRun: Hook<(context: SystemHookContext) -> ()>,

	OuterSystemCall: Hook<(context: SystemCallContext) -> SystemCallHookFn>,
	InnerSystemCall: Hook<(context: SystemCallContext) -> SystemCallHookFn>,
	SystemCall: Hook<(context: SystemCallContext) -> SystemCallHookFn>,

	PhaseAdd: Hook<(context: PhaseContext) -> ()>,
	PhaseBegan: Hook<(context: PhaseContext) -> ()>,
}

--- @prop Hooks { [string]: string }
--- @within Scheduler
--- @since 0.3.0
---
--- See [creating plugins](/docs/plugins/creating).
Scheduler.Hooks = (
	{
		SystemAdd = "SystemAdd",
		SystemRemove = "SystemRemove",
		SystemReplace = "SystemReplace",
		SystemEdited = "SystemEdited",
		SystemCleanup = "SystemCleanup",
		SystemError = "SystemError",
		SystemTriedRun = "SystemTriedRun",

		OuterSystemCall = "OuterSystemCall",
		InnerSystemCall = "InnerSystemCall",
		SystemCall = "SystemCall",

		PhaseAdd = "PhaseAdd",
		PhaseBegan = "PhaseBegan",
	} :: any
) :: Hooks

type HookId = keyof<typeof(Scheduler.Hooks)>

--- @within Scheduler
--- @since 0.3.0
---
--- Allows for registering hooks, see [creating plugins](/docs/plugins/creating).
Scheduler.addHook = function<T, U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, hook: Hook<T>, fn: T)
	local hookId: HookId = hook :: any

	assert(self._hooks[hookId], `Unknown Hook: {hook}`)
	table.insert(self._hooks[hookId], fn)
end

--- @method _addHook
--- @within Scheduler
--- @deprecated 0.3.0 -- Use `Scheduler:addHook()` instead
--- @private
---
--- Internal method for adding hooks maintained for backwards compatibility.
--- Use [Scheduler:addHook] instead.
Scheduler._addHook = Scheduler.addHook

local function callHooks<U...>(
	hooks: Vec<(PartialHookContext) -> unknown>,
	info: PartialHookContext
)
	for _, hook in hooks do
		local success, err = pcall(hook, info)
		if not success then
			warn("Unexpected error in hook:", err)
		end
	end
end

export type SystemHookContext = PartialHookContext & {
	system: SystemInfo<...any>,
}

function Scheduler._systemAdd<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	systemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>
)
	local context = {
		scheduler = self,
		system = systemInfo,
	}

	callHooks(self._hooks["SystemAdd"], context)
end

function Scheduler._systemRemove<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	systemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>
)
	local context: SystemHookContext = {
		scheduler = self,
		system = systemInfo :: any,
	}

	callHooks(self._hooks["SystemRemove"], context)
end

export type SystemReplaceContext = PartialHookContext & {
	new: SystemInfo<...any>,
	old: SystemInfo<...any>,
}

function Scheduler._systemReplace<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	oldSystemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>,
	newSystemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>
)
	local context: SystemReplaceContext = {
		scheduler = self,
		new = newSystemInfo :: any,
		old = oldSystemInfo :: any,
	}

	callHooks(self._hooks["SystemReplace"], context)
end

export type SystemEditedContext = SystemHookContext & {
	old: Phase,
	new: Phase,
}

function Scheduler._systemEdited<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	systemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>,
	old: Phase,
	new: Phase
)
	local context: SystemEditedContext = {
		scheduler = self,
		system = systemInfo :: any,
		new = new,
		old = old,
	}

	callHooks(self._hooks["SystemEdited"], context)
end

export type SystemErrorContext = PartialHookContext & {
	system: SystemInfo<...any>,
	error: SystemLog<unknown>?,
}

function Scheduler._systemCleanup<E, U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	systemInfo,
	cleanupError: SystemLog<E>?
)
	local context: SystemErrorContext = {
		scheduler = self,
		system = systemInfo,
		error = cleanupError,

	callHooks(self._hooks["SystemCleanup"], context)
end

function Scheduler._systemError<E, U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	systemInfo,
	err: SystemLog<E>
)
	local context: SystemErrorContext = {
		scheduler = self,
		system = systemInfo,
		error = err,
	}

	callHooks(self._hooks["SystemError"], context)
end

function Scheduler._systemTriedRun<T, U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, systemInfo)
	local context: SystemHookContext = {
		scheduler = self,
		system = systemInfo,
	}

	callHooks(self._hooks["SystemTriedRun"], context)
end

type SystemHookId = "OuterSystemCall" | "InnerSystemCall" | "SystemCall"

type SystemCallHookFn = () -> ()
type SystemCallCallback = (SystemCallContext) -> SystemCallHookFn
export type SystemCallContext = PartialHookContext & {
	system: SystemInfo<...any>,
	nextFn: SystemCallHookFn,
}

function Scheduler._systemCall<T, U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	hookName: SystemHookId,
	systemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>,
	nextFn: SystemCallHookFn
)
	for _, hook in self._hooks[hookName] :: Vec<SystemCallCallback> do
		local context: SystemCallContext = {
			scheduler = self,
			system = systemInfo :: any,
			nextFn = nextFn,
		}

		nextFn = hook(context)

		if not nextFn then
			local source, line = debug.info(hook, "sl")
			warn(
				`{source}:{line}: Expected 'SystemCall' hook to return a function`
			)
		end
	end

	nextFn()
end

export type PhaseContext = PartialHookContext & {
	phase: Phase,
}

function Scheduler._phaseAdd<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, phase: Phase)
	local context: PhaseContext = {
		scheduler = self,
		phase = phase,
	}

	callHooks(self._hooks["PhaseAdd"], context)
end

function Scheduler._phaseBegan<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, phase: Phase)
	local context: PhaseContext = {
		scheduler = self,
		phase = phase,
	}

	callHooks(self._hooks["PhaseBegan"], context)
end

--- @method getDeltaTime
--- @within Scheduler
--- @return number
---
--- Returns the time since the system was ran last.
--- This must be used within a registered system.
function Scheduler.getDeltaTime<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>)
	if self._currentSystem then
		return self._currentSystem.deltaTime or 0
	end

	local systemFn = debug.info(2, "f")
	if not systemFn or not self._systemInfo[systemFn] then
		error(
			"Scheduler:getDeltaTime() must be used within a registered system"
		)
	end

	return self._systemInfo[systemFn].deltaTime or 0
end

function Scheduler._reportLog<E, U...>(
	_: Scheduler<U...>,
	systemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>,
	log: SystemLog<E>,
	-- A warning after the error providing context
	context: string
)
	local recentLogs = systemInfo.recentLogs
	local logMessage = log.log

	assert(recentLogs)

	if not recentLogs[logMessage] then
		-- LUAU FUTURE: Inference bug
		task.spawn<<(unknown, number)>>(error, logMessage, 0)
		warn(
			`Planck: {context},`
				.. " "
				.. `this error will be ignored for 10 seconds`
		)
		recentLogs[logMessage] = true
	end
end

-- Inspiration from https://github.com/matter-ecs/matter <3
function Scheduler._handleLogs<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	systemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>
)
	if not systemInfo.timeLastLogged then
		systemInfo.timeLastLogged = os.clock()
	end

	if not systemInfo.recentLogs then
		systemInfo.recentLogs = {}
	end

	-- selene: allow(incorrect_standard_library_use)
	do
		assert(systemInfo.timeLastLogged)
		assert(systemInfo.recentLogs)
	end

	if os.clock() - systemInfo.timeLastLogged > 10 then
		systemInfo.timeLastLogged = os.clock()
		systemInfo.recentLogs = {}
	end

	local name = systemInfo.name

	for _, log in systemInfo.logs do
		self:_reportLog(
			systemInfo,
			log,
			`Error occurred in system{string.len(name) > 0 and ` '{name}'` or ""}`
		)
	end

	table.clear(systemInfo.logs)
end

function Scheduler.runSystem<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	system: InternalSystem<U...>,
	justInitialized: boolean
)
	local systemInfo = self._systemInfo[system]
	local now = os.clock()

	if not systemInfo then
		error(
			"Attempted to run a non-registered system, make sure it is added to the Scheduler"
		)
	end

	if justInitialized ~= true then
		if self:_canRun(system) == false then
			self:_systemTriedRun(systemInfo)
			return
		end

		systemInfo.deltaTime = now - (systemInfo.lastTime or now)
	end

	systemInfo.lastTime = now
	self._currentSystem = systemInfo

	if not self._thread then
		self._thread = coroutine.create(function()
			while true do
				local fn = coroutine.yield()
				self._yielded = true
				fn()
				self._yielded = false
			end
		end)

		coroutine.resume(self._thread)
	end

	-- selene: allow(incorrect_standard_library_use)
	assert(self._thread)

	local didYield = false
	local hasSystem = false

	local function systemCall()
		local function noYield()
			local success, errOrSys, cleanup

			coroutine.resume(self._thread, function()
				success, errOrSys, cleanup = xpcall(function()
					return systemInfo.run(table.unpack(self._vargs))
				end, function(e)
					return {
						e = e,
						log = debug.traceback(tostring(e)),
						trace = debug.traceback(),
					}
				end)
			end)

			if success == false then
				didYield = true

				-- selene: allow(incorrect_standard_library_use)
				assert(errOrSys)
				table.insert(systemInfo.logs, errOrSys)
				self:_systemError(systemInfo, errOrSys)

				return
			end

			if self._yielded then
				didYield = true

				local source, line = debug.info(self._thread, 1, "sl")
				local errMessage = `{source}:{line}: System yielded`
				local err = debug.traceback(self._thread, errMessage, 2)

				local log = {
					e = err,
					log = err,
					trace = debug.traceback(self._thread, nil, 2),
				}

				table.insert(systemInfo.logs, log :: SystemLog<unknown>)
				self:_systemError(systemInfo, log)
				return
			end

			if not systemInfo.initialized then
				if errOrSys == nil and cleanup == nil then
					systemInfo.initialized = true
					return
				end

				if type(errOrSys) == "function" then
					systemInfo.run = errOrSys
					systemInfo.initialized = true
					if type(cleanup) == "function" then
						systemInfo.cleanup = cleanup
					end

					hasSystem = true
					return
				end

				if type(errOrSys) == "table" then
					hasSystem = type(errOrSys.system) == "function"
					local hasCleanup = type(errOrSys.cleanup) == "function"

					if hasSystem or hasCleanup then
						if hasSystem then
							systemInfo.run = errOrSys.system
						end

						if hasCleanup then
							systemInfo.cleanup = errOrSys.cleanup
						end

						systemInfo.initialized = true
						return
					end
				end

				local errMessage = `System '{systemInfo.name}' initializer returned invalid type. `
					.. "Expected: function, {system?, cleanup?}, or (function, function). "
					.. `Got: {typeof(errOrSys)}, {typeof(cleanup)}`

				local err = debug.traceback(errMessage)
				local log = {
					e = err,
					log = err,
					trace = debug.traceback(),
				}

				table.insert(systemInfo.logs, log :: SystemLog<unknown>)
				self:_systemError(systemInfo, log)
				systemInfo.initialized = true
			end
		end

		self:_systemCall("SystemCall", systemInfo, noYield)
	end

	local function inner()
		self:_systemCall("InnerSystemCall", systemInfo, systemCall)
	end

	local function outer()
		self:_systemCall("OuterSystemCall", systemInfo, inner)
	end

	if os.clock() - timeLastLogged > 10 then
		timeLastLogged = os.clock()
		recentLogs = {}
	end

	-- LUAU FUTURE: Better types for pcalls
	local success, err = xpcall(outer :: any, function(e)
		return {
			e = e,
			log = debug.traceback(`Error occurred while running hooks: {e}`),
			trace = debug.traceback(),
		}
	end)

	if not success then
		self:_systemError(systemInfo, err)
		self:_reportLog(systemInfo, err, `Error occurred while running hooks`)
	end

	if didYield then
		coroutine.close(self._thread)

		self._thread = coroutine.create(function()
			while true do
				local fn = coroutine.yield()
				self._yielded = true
				fn()
				self._yielded = false
			end
		end)

		coroutine.resume(self._thread)
	end

	self:_handleLogs(systemInfo)
	self._currentSystem = nil

	if hasSystem and justInitialized ~= true then
		self:runSystem(system, true)
	end
end

function Scheduler.runPhase<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, phase: Phase)
	if self:_canRun(phase) == false then
		return
	end

	self:_phaseBegan(phase)

	if not self._phaseToSystems[phase] then
		self._phaseToSystems[phase] = {}
	end

	for _, system in self._phaseToSystems[phase] do
		self:runSystem(system, false)
	end
end

function Scheduler.runPipeline<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, pipeline: Pipeline)
	if self:_canRun(pipeline) == false then
		return
	end

	local orderedList = pipeline.dependencyGraph:getOrderedList()
	assert(
		orderedList,
		`Pipeline {pipeline} contains a circular dependency, check it's Phases`
	)

	for _, phase in orderedList do
		self:runPhase(phase)
	end
end

function Scheduler._canRun<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, dependent: Dependent<U...>)
	local runConditions = self._runIfConditions[dependent :: any]

	if runConditions then
		for _, runIf in runConditions do
			if runIf and not runIf(table.unpack(self._vargs)) then
				return false
			end
		end
	end

	return true
end

--- @method run
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param phase Phase
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Runs all Systems tagged with the Phase in order.

--- @method run
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param pipeline Pipeline
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Runs all Systems tagged with any Phase within the Pipeline in order.

--- @method run
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param system System
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Runs the System, passing in the arguments of the Scheduler, `U...`.
function Scheduler.run<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, dependent: Dependent<U...>)
	assert(
		dependent ~= nil,
		"No dependent specified in Scheduler:run(dependent?)"
	)

	self:runPipeline(Pipeline.Startup)

	if isSystem(dependent) then
		self:runSystem(dependent :: any, false)
	elseif isPhase(dependent) then
		self:runPhase(dependent :: any)
	elseif isPipeline(dependent) then
		self:runPipeline(dependent :: any)
	else
		error("Unknown dependent passed into Scheduler:run(unknown)")
	end

	return self
end

--- @method runAll
--- @within Scheduler
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Runs all Systems within order.
---
--- :::note
--- When you add a Pipeline or Phase with an event, it will be grouped
--- with other Pipelines/Phases on that event. Otherwise, it will be
--- added to the default group.
---
--- When not running systems on Events, such as with the `runAll` method,
--- the Default group will be ran first, and then each Event Group in the
--- order created.
---
--- Pipelines/Phases in these groups are still ordered by their dependencies
--- and by the order of insertion.
--- :::
function Scheduler.runAll<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>)
	local orderedDefaults = self._defaultDependencyGraph:getOrderedList()
	assert(
		orderedDefaults,
		"Default Group contains a circular dependency, check your Pipelines/Phases"
	)

	for _, dependency in orderedDefaults do
		self:run(dependency)
	end

	for identifier, dependencyGraph in self._eventDependencyGraphs do
		local orderedList = dependencyGraph:getOrderedList()
		assert(
			orderedList,
			`Event Group '{identifier}' contains a circular dependency, check your Pipelines/Phases`
		)

		for _, dependency in orderedList do
			self:run(dependency)
		end
	end

	return self
end

type InsertFn =
	& (<U...>(
		self: Scheduler<U...>,
		dependency: Phase | Pipeline
	) -> Scheduler<U...>)
	-- RBXScriptSignal & nil
	& (<U...>(
		self: Scheduler<U...>,
		dependency: Phase | Pipeline,
		signal: RBXScriptSignal<U...>
	) -> Scheduler<U...>)
	-- Instance & RBXScriptSignal
	-- Instance & string
	& (<U...>(
		self: Scheduler<U...>,
		dependency: Phase | Pipeline,
		instance: Instance,
		event: RBXScriptSignal<U...> | string
	) -> Scheduler<U...>)
	-- SignalLike & nil
	& (<U...>(
		self: Scheduler<U...>,
		dependency: Phase | Pipeline,
		signal: SignalLike<U...>
	) -> Scheduler<U...>)

	& (<U...>(
		self: Scheduler<U...>,
		dependency: Phase | Pipeline,
		table: GenericTable,
		event: string
	) -> Scheduler<U...>)

		dependency: Phase | Pipeline,
		instance: GenericTable,
		connectMethod: (GenericTable, Callback<U...>, ...any) -> T
	) -> Scheduler<U...>)

		dependency: Phase | Pipeline,
		connectFn: (Callback<U...>, ...any) -> T
	) -> Scheduler<U...>)

--- @method insert
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param phase Phase
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Initializes the Phase within the Scheduler, ordering it implicitly by
--- setting it as a dependent of the previous Phase/Pipeline.

--- @method insert
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param pipeline Pipeline
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Initializes the Pipeline and it's Phases within the Scheduler,
--- ordering the Pipeline implicitly by setting it as a dependent
--- of the previous Phase/Pipeline.

--- @method insert
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param phase Phase
--- @param instance Instance | EventLike
--- @param event string | EventLike
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Initializes the Phase within the Scheduler, ordering it implicitly
--- by setting it as a dependent of the previous Phase/Pipeline, and
--- scheduling it to be ran on the specified event.
---
--- ```lua
--- local myScheduler = Scheduler.new()
---     :insert(myPhase, RunService, "Heartbeat")
--- ```

--- @method insert
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param pipeline Pipeline
--- @param instance Instance | EventLike
--- @param event string | EventLike
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Initializes the Pipeline and it's Phases within the Scheduler,
--- ordering the Pipeline implicitly by setting it as a dependent of
--- the previous Phase/Pipeline, and scheduling it to be ran on the
--- specified event.
---
--- ```lua
--- local myScheduler = Scheduler.new()
---     :insert(myPipeline, RunService, "Heartbeat")
--- ```
local insertFn: InsertFn = function<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	dependency: Phase | Pipeline,
	instance: any,
	event: any
): Scheduler<U...>
	assert(
		isPhase(dependency) or isPipeline(dependency),
		"Unknown dependency passed to Scheduler:insert(unknown, _, _)"
	)

	if not instance then
		local dependencyGraph = self._defaultDependencyGraph
		dependencyGraph:insertBefore(dependency, self._defaultPhase)
	else
		assert(
			isValidEvent(instance, event),
			"Unknown instance/event passed to Scheduler:insert(_, instance, event)"
		)

		local dependencyGraph = self:_getEventDependencyGraph(instance, event)
		dependencyGraph:insert(dependency)
	end

	if isPhase(dependency) then
		self._phaseToSystems[dependency :: Phase] = {}
		self:_phaseAdd(dependency :: Phase)
	end

	return self
end

Scheduler.insert = insertFn

--- @method insertAfter
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param phase Phase
--- @param after Phase | Pipeline
--- @return Scheduler

--- Initializes the Phase within the Scheduler, ordering it
--- explicitly by setting the after Phase/Pipeline as a dependent.

--- @method insertAfter
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param pipeline Pipeline
--- @param after Phase | Pipeline
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Initializes the Pipeline and it's Phases within the Scheduler,
--- ordering the Pipeline explicitly by setting the after Phase/Pipeline
--- as a dependent.
function Scheduler.insertAfter<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	dependent: Dependency,
	after: Dependency
)
	assert(
		isPhase(after) or isPipeline(after),
		"Unknown dependency passed in Scheduler:insertAfter(_, unknown)"
	)
	assert(
		isPhase(dependent) or isPipeline(dependent),
		"Unknown dependent passed in Scheduler:insertAfter(unknown, _)"
	)

	local dependencyGraph = self:_getGraphOfDependency(after)
	dependencyGraph:insertAfter(dependent, after)

	if isPhase(dependent) then
		self._phaseToSystems[dependent :: Phase] = {}
		self:_phaseAdd(dependent :: Phase)
	end

	return self
end

--- @method addSystem
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param system System
--- @param phase Phase?
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Adds the System to the Scheduler, scheduling it to be ran
--- implicitly within the provided Phase or on the default Main phase.
---
--- **Initializer Systems**: Systems can optionally return a function on their
--- first execution, which becomes the runtime system. This allows one-time
--- setup logic without creating separate initialization phases.
---
--- ```lua
--- local function renderSystem(world, state)
---     -- This runs once on first execution
---     local renderables = world:query(Transform, Model):cached()
---
---     -- This runs on each subsequent execution
---     return function(world, state)
---         for id, transform, model in renderables do
---             render(transform, model)
---         end
---     end, function()
---         -- Optional cleanup logic runs on removeSystem
---     end
--- end
--- ```
function Scheduler.addSystem<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	system: System<U...>,
	phase: Phase?
)
	local systemFn = getSystem(system)
	assert(systemFn, "Unknown system passed to Scheduler:addSystem(unknown, _)")

	local name = getSystemName(system)

	local scheduledPhase
	if phase then
		scheduledPhase = phase
	elseif type(system) == "table" and system.phase then
		scheduledPhase = system.phase
	else
		scheduledPhase = self._defaultPhase
	end

	local systemInfo: SystemInfo<U...> = {
		system = systemFn,
		run = systemFn,
		cleanup = nil,
		phase = scheduledPhase,
		name = name,
		logs = {},
		initialized = false,
	}

	self._systemInfo[systemFn] = systemInfo :: any

	if not self._phaseToSystems[systemInfo.phase] then
		self._phaseToSystems[systemInfo.phase] = {}
	end

	table.insert(
		self._phaseToSystems[systemInfo.phase],
		systemFn :: InternalSystem<...any>
	)

	self:_systemAdd(systemInfo)

	if type(system) == "table" and system.runConditions then
		for _, condition in system.runConditions do
			condition = if typeof(condition) == "table"
				then condition[1]
				else condition
			self:addRunCondition(systemFn, condition)
		end
	end

	return self
end

--- @method addSystems
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param systems { System }
--- @param phase Phase?
---
--- Adds the Systems to the Scheduler, scheduling them to be ran
--- implicitly within the provided Phase or on the default Main phase.
function Scheduler.addSystems<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	systems: { System<U...> },
	phase: Phase?
)
	assert(
		type(systems) == "table",
		"Unknown value passed to Scheduler:addSystems(unknown, _). This value should be an array."
	)

	local foundSystem = false
	local n = 0

	for _, system in systems do
		n += 1
		if getSystem(system) then
			foundSystem = true
			self:addSystem(system, phase)
		end
	end

	assert(n ~= 0, "Empty table passed to Scheduler:addSystems({ }, _)")

	assert(
		foundSystem,
		"Table containing unknown values passed to Scheduler:addSystems({ unknown }, _)"
	)

	return self
end

--- @method editSystem
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param system System
--- @param newPhase Phase
---
--- Changes the Phase that this system is scheduled on.
function Scheduler.editSystem<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	system: System<U...>,
	newPhase: Phase
)
	local systemFn = getSystem(system)
	assert(
		systemFn,
		"Unknown system passed to Scheduler:editSystem(unknown, _)"
	)

	local systemInfo = self._systemInfo[systemFn]
	assert(
		systemInfo,
		"Attempt to edit a non-existent system in Scheduler:editSystem(system, _)"
	)

	assert(
		newPhase and self._phaseToSystems[newPhase] ~= nil or true,
		"Phase never initialized before using Scheduler:editSystem(_, phase)"
	)

	local oldPhase = systemInfo.phase
	local systems = self._phaseToSystems[oldPhase]

	local index = table.find(systems, systemFn :: InternalSystem<...any>)
	assert(index, "Unable to find system within phase")

	table.remove(systems, index)

	if not self._phaseToSystems[newPhase] then
		self._phaseToSystems[newPhase] = {}
	end
	table.insert(
		self._phaseToSystems[newPhase],
		systemFn :: InternalSystem<...any>
	)

	systemInfo.phase = newPhase
	self:_systemEdited(systemInfo :: SystemInfo<U...>, oldPhase, newPhase)

	return self
end

function Scheduler._removeCondition<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	dependent: Dependent<U...>,
	condition: Condition<U...>
)
	self._runIfConditions[dependent :: any] = nil

	for _, _conditions in self._runIfConditions do
		if table.find(_conditions :: any, condition) then
			return
		end
	end

	conditions.cleanupCondition(condition)
end

--- @method removeSystem
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param system System
--- @return Scheduler
---
--- Removes the System from the Scheduler.
---
--- If the system provided a cleanup function during initialization,
--- that cleanup function will be executed before removal.
---
--- ```lua
--- -- System with cleanup
--- local function networkSystem(world, state)
---     local connection = Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
---         -- Player joined logic
---     end)
---
---     return function(world, state)
---         -- Runtime logic
---     end, function()
---         -- Cleanup runs on removeSystem
---         connection:Disconnect()
---     end
--- end
---
--- scheduler:addSystem(networkSystem, Phase.Update)
--- -- Later...
--- scheduler:removeSystem(networkSystem) -- Cleanup executes here
--- ```
function Scheduler.removeSystem<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, system: System<U...>)
	local systemFn = getSystem(system)
	assert(systemFn, "Invalid system passed to Scheduler:removeSystem(system)")

	local systemInfo = self._systemInfo[systemFn]
	assert(
		systemInfo,
		"Attempt to remove a non-existent system in Scheduler:removeSystem(system)"
	)

	if systemInfo.cleanup then
		local success: boolean, err: SystemLog<unknown> = xpcall<<unknown, (nil), (
			SystemLog<unknown>
		)>>(systemInfo.cleanup, function(e)
			local errMessage =
				`Cleanup failed for system '{systemInfo.name}': {e}`

			return {
				e = e,
				log = debug.traceback(errMessage),
				trace = debug.traceback(),
			}
		end, table.unpack(self._vargs))

		if success then
			self:_systemCleanup(systemInfo, nil)
		else
			self:_systemError(systemInfo, err)
			self:_systemCleanup(systemInfo, err)
		end
	end

	local systems = self._phaseToSystems[systemInfo.phase]

	local index = table.find(systems :: any, systemFn)
	assert(index, "Unable to find system within phase")

	table.remove(systems, index)
	self._systemInfo[systemFn] = nil

	if self._runIfConditions[system :: any] then
		for _, condition in self._runIfConditions[system :: any] do
			self:_removeCondition(system, condition)
		end

		self._runIfConditions[system :: any] = nil
	end

	self:_systemRemove(systemInfo :: SystemInfo<U...>)

	return self
end

--- @method replaceSystem
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param old System
--- @param new System
---
--- Replaces the System with a new System.
function Scheduler.replaceSystem<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	old: System<U...>,
	new: System<U...>
)
	local oldSystemFn = getSystem(old) :: InternalSystem<...any>
	assert(
		oldSystemFn,
		"Attempt to pass non-system in Scheduler:replaceSystem(unknown, _)"
	)

	local oldSystemInfo = self._systemInfo[oldSystemFn]
	assert(
		oldSystemInfo,
		"Attempt to replace a non-existent system in Scheduler:replaceSystem(system, _)"
	)

	local newSystemFn = getSystem(new) :: InternalSystem<...any>
	assert(
		newSystemFn,
		"Attempt to pass non-system in Scheduler:replaceSystem(_, unknown)"
	)

	if oldSystemInfo.cleanup then
		-- LUAU FUTURE: Better types for xpcalls
		local success: boolean, err: SystemLog<unknown> = xpcall<<unknown, (nil), (
			SystemLog<unknown>
		)>>(oldSystemInfo.cleanup, function(e)
			local errMessage =
				`Cleanup failed for system '{oldSystemInfo.name}': {e}`

			return {
				e = e,
				log = debug.traceback(errMessage),
				trace = debug.traceback(),
			}
		end, table.unpack(self._vargs))

		if success then
			self:_systemCleanup(oldSystemInfo, nil)
		else
			self:_systemError(oldSystemInfo, err)
			self:_systemCleanup(oldSystemInfo, err)
		end
	end

	local systems = self._phaseToSystems[oldSystemInfo.phase]

	local index = table.find(systems, oldSystemFn)
	assert(index, "Unable to find system within phase")

	table.remove(systems, index)
	table.insert(systems, index, newSystemFn)

	local copy = table.clone(oldSystemInfo)

	oldSystemInfo.system = newSystemFn
	oldSystemInfo.run = newSystemFn
	oldSystemInfo.cleanup = nil
	oldSystemInfo.initialized = false
	oldSystemInfo.name = getSystemName(new)

	self:_systemReplace(
		copy :: SystemInfo<U...>,
		oldSystemInfo :: SystemInfo<U...>
	)

	self._systemInfo[newSystemFn] = self._systemInfo[oldSystemFn]
	self._systemInfo[oldSystemFn] = nil

	return self
end

--- @method addRunCondition
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param system System
--- @param fn (U...) -> any
---
--- Adds a Run Condition which the Scheduler will check before
--- this System is ran.

--- @method addRunCondition
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param phase Phase
--- @param fn (U...) -> any
---
--- Adds a Run Condition which the Scheduler will check before
--- any Systems within this Phase are ran.

--- @method addRunCondition
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param pipeline Pipeline
--- @param fn (U...) -> any
---
--- Adds a Run Condition which the Scheduler will check before
--- any Systems within any Phases apart of this Pipeline are ran.
function Scheduler.addRunCondition<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	dependent: Dependent<U...>,
	fn: Condition<U...>
)
	fn = if typeof(fn) == "table" then fn[1] else fn

	local system: SystemFn<...any>? = getSystem(dependent :: any) :: any
	if system then
		dependent = system
	end

	assert(
		system or isPhase(dependent) or isPipeline(dependent),
		"Attempt to pass unknown dependent into Scheduler:addRunCondition(unknown, _)"
	)

	if not self._runIfConditions[dependent :: any] then
		self._runIfConditions[dependent :: any] = {}
	end

	table.insert(self._runIfConditions[dependent :: any], fn)

	return self
end

function Scheduler._scheduleEvent<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>, instance, event)
	local connect = utils.getConnectFn(instance, event)
	assert(
		connect,
		"Couldn't connect to event as no valid connect methods were found! Ensure the passed event has a 'Connect' or an 'on' method!"
	)

	local identifier = getEventIdentifier(instance, event)

	local dependencyGraph = DependencyGraph.new()

	local callback = function()
		local orderedList = dependencyGraph:getOrderedList()

		if orderedList == nil then
			local err =
				`Event Group '{identifier}' contains a circular dependency, check your Pipelines/Phases`
			if not recentLogs[err] then
				-- LUAU FUTURE: Inference bug
				task.spawn<<(string, number?)>>(error, err, 0)
				warn(
					`Planck: Error occurred while running event, this error will be ignored for 10 seconds`
				)
				recentLogs[err] = true
			end

			return
		end

		for _, dependency in orderedList do
			self:run(dependency :: any)
		end
	end

	self._connectedEvents[identifier] = connect(callback)
	self._eventDependencyGraphs[identifier] =
		dependencyGraph :: DependencyGraph<Dependency>
end

function Scheduler._getEventDependencyGraph<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	instance,
	event
)
	local identifier = getEventIdentifier(instance, event)

	if not self._connectedEvents[identifier] then
		self:_scheduleEvent(instance, event)
	end

	return self._eventDependencyGraphs[identifier]
end

function Scheduler._getGraphOfDependency<U...>(
	self: Scheduler<U...>,
	dependency: Dependency
)
	if table.find(self._defaultDependencyGraph.nodes, dependency) then
		return self._defaultDependencyGraph
	end

	for _, dependencyGraph in self._eventDependencyGraphs do
		if table.find(dependencyGraph.nodes, dependency) then
			return dependencyGraph
		end
	end

	error("Dependency does not belong to a DependencyGraph")
end

--- @within Scheduler
---
--- Disconnects all events, closes all threads, and performs
--- other cleanup work.
---
--- :::danger
--- Only use this if you intend to not use the associated
--- Scheduler anymore. It will not work as intended.
---
--- You should dereference the scheduler object so that
--- it may be garbage collected.
--- :::
---
--- :::warning
--- If you're creating a "throwaway" scheduler, you should
--- not add plugins like Jabby or the Matter Debugger to it.
--- These plugins are unable to properly be cleaned up, use
--- them with caution.
--- :::
function Scheduler.cleanup<U...>(self: Scheduler<U...>)
	for _, connection in self._connectedEvents do
		utils.disconnectEvent(connection)
	end

	for _, plugin in self._plugins do
		-- LUAU FUTURE: Type solver doesn't play nice here
		local cleanup: ((self: Plugin) -> ())? = plugin.cleanup
		if cleanup then
			cleanup(plugin)
		end
	end

	if self._thread then
		coroutine.close(self._thread)
	end

	for _, _conditions in self._runIfConditions do
		for _, condition in _conditions do
			conditions.cleanupCondition(condition)
		end
	end
end

--- @function new
--- @within Scheduler
--- @param args U...
---
--- Creates a new Scheduler, the args passed will be passed to
--- any System anytime it is ran by the Scheduler.
function Scheduler.new<U...>(...: U...): Scheduler<U...>
	local defaultPhase = Phase.new("Default")
	local defaultDependencyGraph: DependencyGraph<Dependency> =
		DependencyGraph.new() :: any

	defaultDependencyGraph:insert(Pipeline.Startup)
	defaultDependencyGraph:insert(defaultPhase)

	local self: Scheduler<U...> = setmetatable({
		_defaultPhase = defaultPhase,
		_defaultDependencyGraph = defaultDependencyGraph,
		_eventDependencyGraphs = {},
		_connectedEvents = {},
		_plugins = {},
		_phaseToSystems = {},
		_hooks = {},
		_runIfConditions = {},
		_systemInfo = {},
		_thread = nil :: any,
		_currentSystem = nil :: any,
		_yielded = false,
		_vargs = { ... },
	}, Scheduler)

	for _, hookName in self.Hooks :: any do
		if not self._hooks[hookName] then
			self._hooks[hookName] = {}
		end
	end

	self:addRunCondition(Pipeline.Startup, conditions.runOnce())
	for _, phase in Pipeline.Startup.dependencyGraph.nodes do
		self:addRunCondition(phase, conditions.runOnce())
	end

	return self :: Scheduler<U...>
end

--- @class Conditions
---
--- Conditions can be used in systems or as Run Conditions.

--- @within Conditions
--- @param time number -- Time in seconds
--- @return hasTimePassed () -> boolean
---
--- A Throttle condition which checks whether the amount of
--- time given has passed or not.
local function timePassed<U...>(time: number): Condition<U...>
	local storedTime: number?

	-- selene: allow(unused_variable)
	return function(...)
		if storedTime == nil or os.clock() - storedTime >= time then
			storedTime = os.clock()
			return true
		end

		return false
	end
end

--- @within Conditions
--- @return hasRanOnce () -> boolean
---
--- Checks whether the condition has been called once before
local function runOnce<U...>(): Condition<U...>
	local hasRan = false

	-- selene: allow(unused_variable)
	return function(...)
		if not hasRan then
			hasRan = true
			return true
		end

		return false
	end
end

end

type OnEventFn =
	-- RBXScriptSignal & nil
	(<U...>(
		RBXScriptSignal<U...>
	) -> (Condition<U...>, CollectEvents<U...>, GetDisconnectFn))
	-- Instance & RBXScriptSignal
	-- Instance & string
	& (<U...>(
		Instance,
		RBXScriptSignal<U...> | string
	) -> (Condition<U...>, CollectEvents<U...>, GetDisconnectFn))

	& (<U...>(
		SignalLike<U...>
	) -> (Condition<U...>, CollectEvents<U...>, GetDisconnectFn))
	-- table & string
	& (<U...>(
		GenericTable,
		string
	) -> (Condition<U...>, CollectEvents<U...>, GetDisconnectFn))
	-- table & connectable method
	& (<T, U...>(
		GenericTable,
		(GenericTable, Callback<U...>, ...any) -> T?
	) -> (Condition<U...>, CollectEvents<U...>, GetDisconnectFn))
	-- connectable function
	& (<T, U...>(
		(Callback<U...>, ...any) -> T?
	) -> (Condition<U...>, CollectEvents<U...>, GetDisconnectFn))

--- @within Conditions
--- @param instance RBXScriptSignal | Instance | SignalLike<...any> | GenericTable | ((Callback<U...>,...any) -> ...any)
--- @param event (RBXScriptSignal | string | (...any) -> ())?
--- @return hasNewEvent () -> boolean
--- @return collectEvents () -> () -> (number, U...)
--- @return getDisconnectFn () -> () -> ()
---
--- Checks for any new events and allows for the collection of
--- those events.\
--- \
--- Read [OnEvent](../docs/design/conditions#on-event) for more information.
local function onEvent<U...>(
	instance,
	event
): (Condition<U...>, CollectEvents<U...>, (
) -> () -> ())
	local connect = getConnectFn(instance, event)
	assert(connect, "Event passed to .onEvent is not valid")

	local newEvent = false
	local queue: { { any } } = {}

	local connection: ConnectionLike?

	local function disconnect()
		if not connection then
			return
		end

		utils.disconnectEvent(connection)
		connection = nil
	end

	local function callback(...)
		newEvent = true
		table.insert(queue, { ... })
	end

	connection = connect(callback)

	local function hasNewEvent()
		if newEvent then
			newEvent = false
			return true
		end

		table.clear(queue)
		return false
	end

	local function collectEvents()
		local n = 0
		return function(): (number, U...)
			n += 1

			local args = table.remove(queue, 1)

			if args then
				return n, table.unpack(args)
			end

			return nil :: any
		end
	end

	local function getDisconnectFn()
		return disconnect
	end

	conditionToCleanupFn[hasNewEvent] = disconnect

	return hasNewEvent, collectEvents, getDisconnectFn
end

	return function(...)
		return not condition(...)
	end
end

	{ "disconnect", "Disconnect", "destroy", "Destroy" }

local function disconnectEvent(connection: ConnectionLike)
	if type(connection) == "function" then
		connection()
		return
	elseif typeof(connection) == "RBXScriptConnection" then
		connection:Disconnect()
		return
	elseif type(connection) == "table" then
		for _, method in EVENT_DISCONNECT_METHODS do
			local connect: unknown = (connection :: any)[method]

			if connect and connect == "function" then
				(connect :: any)(connection)
				return

		end
	end
end

type GetConnectFn =
	-- RBXScriptSignal & nil
	(<U...>(RBXScriptSignal<U...>) -> ConnectFn<RBXScriptConnection, U...>)
	-- Instance & RBXScriptSignal
	-- Instance & string
	& (<U...>(
		Instance,
		RBXScriptSignal<U...> | string
	) -> ConnectFn<RBXScriptConnection, U...>)
	-- SignalLike & nil
	& (<U...>(SignalLike<U...>) -> ConnectFn<any, U...>)
	-- table & string
	& (<U...>(GenericTable, string) -> ConnectFn<any, U...>)
	-- table & connectable method
	& (<T, U...>(
		GenericTable,
		(GenericTable, Callback<U...>, ...any) -> T
	) -> ConnectFn<T, U...>)
	-- connectable function

-- This function is inspired by useEvent in Matter, a library by evaera (https://github.com/evaera)
-- License: Copyright (c) 2021 Eryn L. K., MIT License
-- Source: https://github.com/matter-ecs/matter/blob/main/lib/hooks/useEvent.luau
local getConnectFn: GetConnectFn = function(instance: any, event: any): any
	local eventInstance = instance

	if typeof(event) == "RBXScriptSignal" or type(event) == "table" then
		eventInstance = event
	elseif type(event) == "string" then
		eventInstance = (instance :: any)[event]
	end

	if type(eventInstance) == "function" then
		return eventInstance
	elseif typeof(eventInstance) == "RBXScriptSignal" then
		return function(callback)
			return eventInstance:Connect(callback)
		end
	end

	if type(eventInstance) == "table" then
		if type(event) == "function" then
			return function(callback)
				return (event :: any)(eventInstance, callback)
			end
		end

		for _, method in EVENT_CONNECT_METHODS do
			if type(eventInstance[method]) ~= "function" then
				continue
			end

			return function(callback)
				return eventInstance[method](eventInstance, callback)
			end
		end
	end

	return nil
end

local function isValidEvent(instance, event)
	return getConnectFn(instance, event) ~= nil
end

local n = 0

local STARTUP_PHASES = { "PreStartup", "Startup", "PostStartup" }

local function isStartup<U...>(phase: Phase)
	return table.find(STARTUP_PHASES, phase._name) ~= nil
end

function Plugin.build(_: Plugin, scheduler: Scheduler<...unknown>)
	n += 1

	local identifier = n > 1 and ` #{n}` or ""
	local name = `Planck{identifier}`

	local jabbyScheduler = Jabby.scheduler.create()
	local startupScheduler = Jabby.scheduler.create()

	local systemToId = {}

	local function addSystem<U...>(
		systemFn: InternalSystem<U...>,
		systemInfo: SystemInfo<U...>
	)
		if isStartup(systemInfo.phase) then
			local id = startupScheduler:register_system({
				name = systemInfo.name,
				phase = tostring(systemInfo.phase),
			})

			startupScheduler:set_system_data(id, {
				paused = true,
			})
			systemToId[systemFn] = id
		else
			local id = jabbyScheduler:register_system({
				name = systemInfo.name,
				phase = tostring(systemInfo.phase),
			})

			jabbyScheduler:set_system_data(id, {
				paused = true,
			})
			systemToId[systemFn] = id
		end
	end

	for systemFn, systemInfo in scheduler._systemInfo do
		addSystem(systemFn, systemInfo)
	end

	scheduler:addHook(
		scheduler.Hooks.SystemAdd,
		function(context: SystemHookContext)
			local systemInfo = context.system
			addSystem(systemInfo.system, systemInfo)
		end
	)

	scheduler:addHook(
		scheduler.Hooks.SystemRemove,
		function(context: SystemHookContext)
			local systemInfo = context.system
			local system = systemInfo.system

			if isStartup(systemInfo.phase) then
				startupScheduler:remove_system(systemToId[system])
			else
				jabbyScheduler:remove_system(systemToId[system])
			end

			systemToId[system] = nil
		end
	)

	scheduler:addHook(
		scheduler.Hooks.SystemReplace,
		function(context: SystemReplaceContext)
			local newSystemInfo = context.new
			local oldSystemInfo = context.old
			local newSystem = newSystemInfo.system
			local oldSystem = context.old.system

			-- Scheduler:replaceSystem() does not change the phase
			if isStartup(oldSystemInfo.phase) then
				startupScheduler:remove_system(systemToId[oldSystem])
				systemToId[oldSystem] = nil

				local id = jabbyScheduler:register_system({
					name = newSystemInfo.name,
					phase = tostring(newSystemInfo.phase),
				})

				systemToId[newSystem] = id
			else
				jabbyScheduler:remove_system(systemToId[oldSystem])
				systemToId[oldSystem] = nil

				local id = jabbyScheduler:register_system({
					name = newSystemInfo.name,
					phase = tostring(newSystemInfo.phase),
				})

				systemToId[newSystem] = id
			end
		end
	)

	scheduler:addHook(
		scheduler.Hooks.SystemEdited,
		function(context: SystemEditedContext)
			local systemInfo = context.system
			local system = systemInfo.system
			local newPhase = context.new
			local oldPhase = context.old

			if isStartup(oldPhase) then
				startupScheduler:set_system_data(systemToId[system], {
					phase = tostring(newPhase),
				})
			else
				jabbyScheduler:set_system_data(systemToId[system], {
					phase = tostring(newPhase),
				})
			end
		end
	)

	scheduler:addHook(
		scheduler.Hooks.SystemTriedRun,
		function(context: SystemHookContext)
			local systemInfo = context.system
			local system = systemInfo.system

			local id = systemToId[system]

			if isStartup(systemInfo.phase) then
				startupScheduler:set_system_data(id, {
					paused = true,
				})
			else
				jabbyScheduler:set_system_data(id, {
					paused = true,
				})
			end
		end
	)

	scheduler:addHook(
		scheduler.Hooks.SystemCall,
		function(context: SystemCallContext)
			local systemInfo = context.system
			local system = systemInfo.system

			local id = systemToId[system]

			return function()
				if isStartup(systemInfo.phase) then
					startupScheduler:set_system_data(id, {
						paused = false,
					})
					startupScheduler:run(id, function()
						context.nextFn()
					end)
				else
					jabbyScheduler:set_system_data(id, {
						paused = false,
					})
					jabbyScheduler:run(id, function()
						context.nextFn()
					end)
				end
			end
		end
	)

	Jabby.register({
		applet = Jabby.applets.scheduler,
		name = name .. " (Startup)",
		configuration = {
			scheduler = startupScheduler,
		},
	})

	Jabby.register({
		applet = Jabby.applets.scheduler,
		name = name,
		configuration = {
			scheduler = jabbyScheduler,
		},
	})
end

			part ..= `\n{string.rep("  ", _depth - 1)}`

		elseif luaType == "boolean" then

		elseif luaType == "table" then
			if mode == FormatMode.Short then
				part ..= "{..}"
			else
				part ..= formatTable(
					value,
					FormatMode.Long,
					#str + #part + _padLength,
					_depth + 1,
					_seen

			if count > 1 then

		else

		end

		str ..= `\n{string.rep("  ", _depth - 2)}`
	end

	if mode == FormatMode.Short or _depth > 1 then
		str ..= "}"
	end

	it always returns the *same* table, based on the script and line where *your function* (the function calling

	### Uniqueness

	If your function is called multiple times from the same line, perhaps within a loop, the default behavior of
	`useHookState` is to uniquely identify these by call count, and will return a unique table for each call.

	However, you can override this behavior: you can choose to key by any other value. This means that in addition to
	script and line number, the storage will also only return the same table if the unique value (otherwise known as the

	As a second optional parameter, you can pass a function that is automatically invoked when your storage is about
	to be cleaned up. This happens when your function (and by extension, `useHookState`) ceases to be called again
	next frame (keyed by script, line number, and discriminator).

	like disconnecting events.

	around another frame (even if your function wasn't called again). This can be used when you know that the user will
	(or might) eventually call your function again, even if they didn't this frame. (For example, caching a value for
	a number of seconds).

	or the user actually calls your function again.

	local function cleanup(storage)

	discriminator: any?,
	cleanupCallback: ((storage: T) -> boolean)?

	local fn = debug.info(2, "f")

	local baseKey = string.format("%s:%s:%d", tostring(fn), file, line)

	local currentFrame = stack[#stack]

	if currentFrame == nil then
		error(
			"Attempt to access topologically-aware storage outside of a Loop-system context.",
			3
		)

	if not currentFrame.accessedKeys[baseKey] then
		currentFrame.accessedKeys[baseKey] = {}
	end

	local accessedKeys = currentFrame.accessedKeys[baseKey]

	local key = #accessedKeys

	if discriminator ~= nil then
		if type(discriminator) == "number" then
			discriminator = tostring(discriminator)
		end

		key = discriminator
	end

	accessedKeys[key] = true

	if not currentFrame.node.system[baseKey] then
		currentFrame.node.system[baseKey] = {
			storage = {},
			cleanupCallback = cleanupCallback,
		}
	end

	local storage = currentFrame.node.system[baseKey].storage

	if not storage[key] then
		storage[key] = {}
	end

	return storage[key]

		return eventObject:Connect(callback)
	end

	if type(eventObject) == "table" then
		for _, method in EVENT_CONNECT_METHODS do
			if type(eventObject[method]) ~= "function" then
				continue
			end

			return eventObject[method](eventObject, callback)
		end
	end

	error(
		"Couldn't connect to event as no valid connect methods were found! Ensure the passed event has a 'Connect' or an 'on' method!"
	)
end

local function disconnect(connection)
	if connection == nil then
		return
	end

	if type(connection) == "function" then
		connection()
		return
	end

	for _, method in CONNECTION_DISCONNECT_METHODS do
		if type(connection[method]) ~= "function" then
			continue
		end

		connection[method](connection)
		break
	end
end

local function validateConnection(connection)
	if
		typeof(connection) == "function"
		or typeof(connection) == "RBXScriptConnection"
	then
		return
	end

	for _, method in CONNECTION_DISCONNECT_METHODS do
		if type(connection) ~= "table" or connection[method] == nil then
			continue
		end

		return
	end

	error(
		"Ensure passed event returns a cleanup function, or a table with a 'Disconnect' or a 'Destroy' method!"
	)
end

local function cleanup(storage)
	disconnect(storage.connection)
	storage.queue = nil
end

--[=[
	@within Matter
	@ignore
	:::info Topologically-aware function
	This function is only usable if called within the context of [`Loop:begin`](/api/Loop#begin).
	:::

	Collects events that fire during the frame and allows iteration over event arguments.

	```lua
	for _, player in ipairs(Players:GetPlayers()) do
		for i, character in useEvent(player, "CharacterAdded") do
			world:spawn(
				Components.Target(),
				Components.Model({
					model = character,
				})
			)
		end
	end
	```

	Returns an iterator function that returns an ever-increasing number, starting at 1, followed by any event arguments
	from the specified event.

	Events are returned in the order that they were fired.

	:::caution
	`useEvent` keys storage uniquely identified by **the script and line number** `useEvent` was called from, and the
	first parameter (instance). If the second parameter, `event`, is not equal to the event passed in for this unique
	storage last frame, the old event is disconnected from and the new one is connected in its place.

	Tl;dr: on a given line, you should hard-code a single event to connect to. Do not dynamically change the event with
	a variable. Dynamically changing the first parameter (instance) is fine.

	```lua
	for _, instance in pairs(someTable) do
		for i, arg1, arg2 in useEvent(instance, "Touched") do -- This is ok
		end
	end

	for _, instance in pairs(someTable) do
		local event = getEventSomehow()
		for i, arg1, arg2 in useEvent(instance, event) do -- PANIC! This is NOT OK
		end
	end
	```
	:::

	If `useEvent` ceases to be called on the same line with the same instance and event, the event connection is
	disconnected from automatically.

	You can also pass the actual event object instead of its name as the second parameter:

	```lua
	useEvent(instance, instance.Touched)
	useEvent(instance, instance:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Name"))
	```

	`useEvent` supports custom events as well, so you can pass in an object with a `Connect`, `connect` or an `on` method.
	The object returned by any event must either be a cleanup function, or a table with a `Disconnect` or a `Destroy`
	method so that `useEvent` can later clean the event up when needed.	See [ConnectionObject] for more information.

	@param instance Instance | { [string]: CustomEvent } | CustomEvent -- The instance or the custom event, or a table that has the event you want to connect to
	@param event string | RBXScriptSignal | CustomEvent -- The name of, or the actual event that you want to connect to
]=]
local function useEvent(
	instance: Instance | { [string]: CustomEvent } | CustomEvent,
	event: string | RBXScriptSignal | CustomEvent
): () -> (number, ...any)
	assert(instance ~= nil, "Instance is nil")
	assert(event ~= nil, "Event is nil")

	local storage = topoRuntime.useHookState(instance, cleanup)

	if storage.event ~= event then
		if storage.event then
			disconnect(storage.connection)
			warn("useEvent event changed:", storage.event, "->", event)
			table.clear(storage)
		end

		local queue = Queue.new()
		storage.queue = queue
		storage.event = event

		local connection = connect(instance, function(...)
			queue:pushBack(table.pack(...))
		end, event)

		validateConnection(connection)
		storage.connection = connection
	end

	local index = 0
	return function(): any
		index += 1

		local arguments = storage.queue:popFront()

		if arguments then
			return index, unpack(arguments, 1, arguments.n)
		end
		return
	end
end

return useEvent

	Utility for easy time-based throttling.

	Accepts a duration, and returns `true` if it has been that long since the last time this function returned `true`.
	Always returns `true` the first time.

	This function returns unique results keyed by script and line number. Additionally, uniqueness can be keyed by a
	unique value, which is passed as a second parameter. This is useful when iterating over a query result, as you can
	throttle doing something to each entity individually.

	```lua
	if useThrottle(1) then -- Keyed by script and line number only
		print("only prints every second")
	end

	for id, enemy in world:query(Enemy) do
		if useThrottle(5, id) then -- Keyed by script, line number, and the entity id
			print("Recalculate target...")
		end
	end
	```

	@param discriminator? any -- A unique value to additionally key by
	@return boolean -- returns true every x seconds, otherwise false
]=]
local function useThrottle(seconds: number, discriminator: any?): boolean
	local storage = topoRuntime.useHookState(discriminator, cleanup)

	if storage.time == nil or os.clock() - storage.time >= seconds then
		storage.time = os.clock()
		storage.expiry = os.clock() + seconds
		return true
	end

	return false
end

return useThrottle
